name: CostBar
subtitle: AI API cost & budget monitor
promotional_text: Keep account costs, dated credits and API eligibility separate. See expiry, record plan allowance observations, and export a redacted report.
description:
CostBar shows reported AI API costs in your menu bar. With your own credentials, you can connect OpenRouter, Anthropic or OpenAI to read cost reports without making inference requests, then check the reported costs from each provider separately because their billing reports cover different things.

You can see daily and monthly spend in USD, plus today's average spend per hour. Set a monthly budget for each provider and choose when to receive an alert. Budgets are reminders and don't stop spending. The month-end forecast is an estimate, so check your provider's billing dashboard for charges.

Provider totals cover different things. OpenRouter reports the saved key's spend and can show account credits with a management key. Anthropic and OpenAI require organization admin keys to read organization costs, and Anthropic's report excludes Priority Tier costs. Reports may arrive late, and periods use UTC.

Forecasts wait for at least three days and ten percent of the UTC month, and stay hidden while reports update or when data is incomplete or stale.

Try Sample mode without a key or network request. You can also test a demo key in a separate Keychain item and send a labeled Sample notification. Real keys stay in the system Keychain, while cached totals and settings stay on your computer. Launch at Login is optional and off by default.

Accounts & Credits keeps multiple accounts from the same provider separate. Add a manual-only account without a key. Record dated credit grants, expiry and explicit workload eligibility. The selected-workload total excludes expired, future-dated and ineligible grants. Monthly Max API promotions cannot fund ordinary API-funded Claude Code. Manual records are not provider-verified and do not guarantee that a request will succeed.

Keep debt, reported USD spend and subscription allowance percentages separate. Each connected reporting account has its own key, cached observation and failure status. Unavailable accounts retain their last dated report with a historical label.

Import a selected local JSON Lines file for a token estimate against your own budget. The app stores aggregate counts rather than raw logs or paths. This estimate is not billed spend or an official provider quota. Export a local redacted JSON report with typed facts and salted account pseudonyms. It omits keys, display names, free-text notes, URLs and file paths. Financial figures can still be sensitive; review before sharing.

review_notes:
Build 3 substantially extends the rejected build 2. This is the substantial-changes route, not a claim that build 2 already complied. No private account is needed for the demonstrations below.

NEW WORKFLOW. Launch CostBar, click its menu bar icon, then choose Open in Accounts & credits. Choose Load synthetic sample. Select Team A and choose Agent SDK. eligible manual grants total $140, excluding the expired $25. Choose API-funded Claude Code. $0, because those grants do not cover that workload. Choose Subscription use. no USD total; the separate 62.5% observation stays visible. Team B demonstrates a rejected reporting key with its last dated report retained as historical. All figures are labelled synthetic.

Exit Sample mode and choose Add account > Manual records only. No key is needed. Record a grant's remaining balance, source date, expiry and explicit workload eligibility. Unknown or expired eligibility never counts. Debt, reported spend and subscription percentages stay separate. Adding a reporting key is optional. Each account has its own identity, key and cached report.

Import log file uses the native chooser for a selected JSON Lines file of at most 5 MB. It retains only token aggregates, with counting-method limits, not the raw log or path. It never presents the estimate as billed spend or an official quota. Export redacted report uses the native Save panel; it contains typed facts and salted account pseudonyms, excluding keys, names, paths and free-text notes.

ORIGINAL PROVIDER VIEW. Choose Try with sample data in the empty state or Settings (Command-comma) > General. Select each provider. OpenRouter includes Account credits left. Fill sample key tests a separate demo Keychain item. Send Sample notification requests macOS permission and a labelled local test notification. Sample mode uses no real account or provider request. Live reports require the provider's documented reporting access; no inference calls are made. Budgets are reminders and do not stop spending.

PORTFOLIO. The useful local-log estimate was consolidated into CostBar. A separate QuotaPace release is on hold. Related apps and shared code are disclosed in the review evidence. CostBar uses internal MASKit launch/smoke helpers, its own domain logic and screenshot composer, and Apple frameworks. Development used automated coding tools. The internal Barframe plan defined the product, providers, price and name under the Michael Lip team; the project records identify no outside client content supplier.

TESTING. Documented testing is automated and agent-operated synthetic QA. No external beta feedback is claimed. The current Apple beta-group, tester and feedback lists are empty. This does not prove a complete historical absence of off-platform testing.

Privacy Policy and Support are available in the app and at the configured barframe.com URLs. com.apple.security.network.client permits read-only provider reports. com.apple.security.files.user-selected.read-write permits selected log import and local report export. Keys use Keychain; raw logs are not uploaded. Launch at login is optional and off by default.

Review attachment. CostBar-Build-3-Review-Evidence.pdf gives all nine factual answers, the related product inventory, consolidation decision, and build 3 workflow images.
whats_new: First release candidate. separate account reports; dated manual credit eligibility and expiry; separate debt and subscription observations; local token estimates and redacted report export.
